question: The Afghan noble Khan Jahan Lodi rebelled against the Mughal emperor ___________ and was defeated.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Khan Jahan Lodi was an Afghan noble who served under the Mughal emperor **Shah Jahan**.

• He was appointed as the governor of the Deccan by Shah Jahan.

• Khan Jahan Lodi later rebelled against Shah Jahan due to political differences and ambitions of independence.

• He was eventually defeated and killed by the Mughal forces in 1631.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Shah Jahan**

• Shah Jahan, whose reign lasted from 1628 to 1658, is best known for his architectural achievements, most notably the construction of the Taj Mahal.

• He was the fifth Mughal emperor and the son of Emperor Jahangir.

• During his reign, the Mughal Empire reached its cultural zenith.

• Shah Jahan's period is often regarded as the golden age of Mughal architecture, with monumental structures like the Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi.

• **Mughal Empire**

• The Mughal Empire was a prominent empire in South Asia that lasted from the early 16th to the mid-19th century.

• It was known for its rich cultural contributions, including art, architecture, and literature.

• The Mughal rulers were of Turko-Mongol origin and they established a centralized and efficient administrative system.

• The empire played a significant role in the spread of Islam in the Indian subcontinent.

• **Deccan Region**

• The Deccan region refers to the plateau in the southern part of India, which is bounded by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats mountain ranges.

• Historically, the Deccan has been a strategic and contested region due to its location and resources.

• The region saw various dynasties and rulers, including the Bahmani Sultanate and later the Mughal expansion under Shah Jahan.

• The Deccan was known for its distinct culture and contributions to Indian history, including unique architectural styles and literature.
